shifted_share.status: SOURCED 2026-10-06. Two independent estimates on the SAME denominator, the share of the foreign profits of US multinationals booked in tax havens. No longer swept over a judgement range.
shifted_share.bound: a share. The range spans both sourced estimates and the stated imprecision of the second: Torslov, Wier and Zucman give 0.48 for 2016 from the BEA value added tables, and Garcia-Bernardo, Jansky and Zucman give 'around 50 percent, stable between 2015 and 2020' from survey, tax and firm financial data, read here as 0.50 plus or minus 0.03.
sources: Torslov, Wier and Zucman, The Missing Profits of Nations: 'In 2016, according to the BEA Value Added tables, 48% of the pre-tax profit of majority-owned affiliates of US multinationals were made in tax havens.'
Garcia-Bernardo, Jansky and Zucman, NBER w30086, abstract verified verbatim 2026-10-06: 'The share of foreign profits booked in tax havens remained stable around 50% between 2015 and 2020.'
shifted_share.correction: The earlier note sought 'Clausing (NBER w28442)'. NBER w28442 is Solar Geoengineering, Learning, and Experimentation; it is not a profit-shifting paper and the number was wrong.
shifted_share.DENOMINATOR_CAVEAT: Both estimates are shares of FOREIGN profits. assemble.py applies this parameter to the whole rent base, so a dollar of US rent is treated as booked abroad with this probability. That overstates shifting unless essentially all rent is earned through foreign affiliates, and correcting it would RAISE tau_k and NARROW the measured shortfall. Reported as a limitation, not silently changed.
